newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's PRI, PAN in near tie in Nuevo Leon poll.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's PRI, PAN in near tie in Nuevo Leon poll.

text.p: A poll published on Friday showed Mexico's ruling party with a slight lead over the conservative opposition in northern Nuevo Leon state, but the two parties are in a virtual tie considering the margin of error.

The industrial border state of Nuevo Leon is one of six Mexican states that will chose a governor on July 6, the same day that Mexicans will elect all 500 members of the lower house, one-fourth of the Senate and a mayor for Mexico City.
The poll published by the Monterrey newspaper El Norte showed the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) with 37 percent support compared to 35 percent for the National Action Party.
The poll, conducted among 990 people from May 27 to June 4, has a margin of error of plus or minus three points, El Norte said.
The PAN slipped from 36 percent in the previous El Norte poll a month earlier, when the PRI registered the same 37 percent.

In the race for governor of Nuevo Leon, PRI candidate Natividad Gonzalez Parras maintained his level of support of 38.8 percent, while PAN candidate Fernando Canales Clariond fell to 35.6 percent from 36.4 percent a month earlier, El Norte said.
Gonzalez overtook the lead from Canales in April after having trailed badly, 43.3 percent to 26.8 percent, back in December.
